# Shell integration

Source: https://unterm.app/docs/shell-integration

A terminal sees bytes. Shell integration is the shell telling it what those bytes are: here a prompt begins, here the command line ends, here a command starts running, here it finished with exit status 2. Those are the `OSC 133` marks (`A`, `B`, `C`, `D;<status>`), plus `OSC 7` for the working directory.

Unterm uses them to:

- mark a tab whose last command **failed** (non-zero exit) with the sidebar's ▲, and *not* mark one whose output merely contains the word "error";
- jump between prompts in the scrollback;
- split a [recording](/docs/configuration) into commands;
- clear a program's progress bar when its prompt returns.

## What Unterm does

When Unterm starts zsh, bash, fish or PowerShell, it loads a small script into it. Your own files are read exactly as they would be anywhere else.

| Shell | How the script is loaded |
|---|---|
| zsh | `ZDOTDIR` points at Unterm's `.zshenv`, which puts your own `ZDOTDIR` back first, sources your `.zshenv`, and adds `precmd`/`preexec` hooks. zsh then reads your `.zprofile` and `.zshrc` as usual. |
| bash | Started with `--rcfile`, a file that reads the login files (`/etc/profile`, then the first of `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.bash_login`, `~/.profile`) for a login shell, or `~/.bashrc` otherwise, and then adds the marks through `PROMPT_COMMAND`, `PS1` and `PS0`. No `DEBUG` trap, so yours or bash-preexec's is left alone. |
| fish | A `vendor_conf.d` script found through `XDG_DATA_DIRS`. |
| PowerShell | `-NoExit -Command ". unterm.ps1"`, which wraps the prompt your profile set. The command-start mark is added to Enter only while Enter still does what PSReadLine ships with. |

A shell given arguments of its own — `bash -c "…"`, `pwsh -File build.ps1` — is running something specific and is left alone. So is every other program.

The scripts are built into Unterm and written to `~/.unterm/shell-integration/` the first time they are needed.

## Turning it off

```ini
shell_integration = false
```

in `~/.unterm/unterm.conf`, and new shells start exactly as configured.

## Remote shells

Integration is loaded into shells Unterm starts. A shell on another machine reached through `ssh` does not get it; to have the marks there, source the matching script from `~/.unterm/shell-integration/` in that machine's startup file.


---

# Unterm v0.55: the Agent Cockpit

Source: https://unterm.app/blog/agent-cockpit-v055

If you run AI coding agents all day, you know the actual bottleneck isn't the model. It's you, alt-tabbing across panes to find out which agent finished, which one has been silently waiting twenty minutes for a `y`, and what exactly any of them did to your repo.

Unterm v0.55 makes the terminal answer those questions itself. We call it the **Agent Cockpit**.

## Who's doing what, at a glance

Every pane that hosts an agent — Claude Code, Codex CLI, Gemini CLI, Aider, and friends — now carries a live state: **working** (breathing blue dot on the tab), **needs you** (amber), **done** (green), **idle** (grey). The top bar keeps a cross-window tally that flips amber the instant any agent blocks on you.

Detection is zero-config for Claude Code and Gemini CLI: Unterm reads the signals agents already emit — title spinners, OSC progress sequences, desktop-notification escapes. One command, `unterm-cli agent enable-hooks`, upgrades Claude Code, Codex, and Aider to exact hook-level reporting (merge-only config writes, `.unterm-bak` backups, your existing settings untouched).

## The Inbox: stop hunting for blocked agents

`Ctrl+Shift+A` opens the Agent Inbox: every agent across every window, sorted **waiting-first**, with how long it's been stuck and what it's working on. Enter jumps to the pane. The most common multi-agent action — "go press y somewhere" — is now two keystrokes.

## Fleet: race three agents on the same task

```
unterm-cli fleet launch --agents claude,claude,codex -- fix the login bug
```

Each member gets its own git worktree (beside your repo, on its own branch — your working copy is never touched), its own tab, and its own state badge. Crew presets come from whatever agents you actually have installed, including `claude + codex + gemini` for a proper three-model bake-off.

## Review: nothing an agent does is untracked

The moment an agent starts working in a repo, Unterm snapshots the worktree as a dangling commit — HEAD, index, and files untouched, so you'll never notice it happened until you need it. The new **Review** page shows line-level diffs (including files the agent created), squash-merges the take you like into your repo as *staged* changes — the commit stays yours — discards the takes you don't, rolls any repo back to any checkpoint, and puts two fleet members' diffs side by side.

## Also in this release

- CJK input methods now work correctly in every palette — composition previews inline instead of vanishing (this one was found by our own daily dogfooding, ten minutes after shipping the palettes).
- OSC 9 / OSC 777 notifications now actually reach window-level consumers.
- Sidebar no longer rebuilds ~44ms per title-spinner frame while an agent works — a real CPU saving for anyone running agents for hours.

## The thesis, completed

Unterm's founding idea is *"the terminal AI agents can drive"* — every window is an MCP server that external agents operate. The cockpit is the same idea pointed inward: the agents running in your panes are now first-class citizens the terminal understands. And true to that thesis, the cockpit itself is fully scriptable — 12 new MCP methods and three new CLI command families mean an orchestrating agent can launch fleets and review diffs without a human in the chair.

Free, MIT, local-first, no accounts, no telemetry. [Download v0.55](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/releases/latest) · [Agent Cockpit docs](/docs/agent-cockpit)

---

# Live ⭐ + ↓ on a static product site, three layers

Source: https://unterm.app/blog/live-stats-three-layer

## Why naive doesn't work

You'd think you could just slap an `await fetch("https://api.github.com/repos/<you>/<repo>")` into your hero section and be done. Three reasons that breaks:

1. **Rate limit.** The unauth GitHub API is 60 requests per hour per IP. A modestly-trafficked landing page eats that in seconds — and the user behind a CGNAT'd home network sees `403 forbidden` on first paint while their neighbor's request was the 61st of the hour.
2. **CORS gotchas.** api.github.com sends sane CORS headers, but Safari Private mode, some corporate proxies, and content blockers strip them. The fetch errors out and your hero shows `undefined`.
3. **First-paint latency.** If the number arrives 600 ms after the page is interactive, social-media preview cards (Twitter, Slack, RSS) all see it blank. So do crawlers. So does the user on a 3G connection.

## The three layers

The architecture answers each failure mode with its own layer:

| Layer | What it solves | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| **1. Build-time SSR** | Numbers are baked into the HTML. Crawlers, OG cards, RSS, Reader Mode, JS-disabled all see them. | — |
| **2. Edge proxy `/api/stats`** | Visitors only ever talk to your domain. Each region's edge cache talks to GitHub once every 5 minutes, regardless of traffic. | SSR's stale numbers |
| **3. Client refresh** | A page deployed last week still shows today's numbers. The hero updates after first paint, no flicker. | SSR's stale numbers |

Each upper layer is independent — if Layer 2 is down, Layer 1's numbers are still on screen. If Layer 3 fails, Layer 1 (or 2) stays. There's no single point of failure in the path that ends with "user sees a blank chip".

## Layer 1 — Build-time SSR

Run during the static-site build. We're using Astro 4 here but the pattern is the same in Next/Nuxt/SvelteKit/Hugo — anywhere you can run code at build time and bake the result into HTML.

```ts
// web/src/lib/stats.ts
const REPO = "zhitongblog/unterm";

export interface Stats {
  // null means "no trustworthy answer yet" — render as em dash, not 0.
  // Distinguishing null vs 0 is load-bearing: a transient GitHub 503 must
  // not pin "⭐ 0 stars" onto the homepage for the next 5 minutes.
  stars: number | null;
  downloads: number | null;
  release: string;
}

let cache: Promise<Stats> | null = null;
export function fetchStats(): Promise<Stats> {
  if (!cache) cache = doFetch();
  return cache;
}

async function doFetch(): Promise<Stats> {
  try {
    const [r1, r2] = await Promise.all([
      fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${REPO}`),
      fetch(`https://api.github.com/repos/${REPO}/releases?per_page=100`),
    ]);
    if (!r1.ok || !r2.ok) return FALLBACK;
    const repo = await r1.json();
    const releases = await r2.json();
    const downloads = releases.reduce((s: number, r: any) =>
      s + r.assets.reduce((a: number, x: any) => a + (x.download_count ?? 0), 0), 0);
    return {
      stars: repo.stargazers_count ?? null,
      downloads: releases.length > 0 ? downloads : null,
      release: releases[0]?.tag_name ?? "v0.14",
    };
  } catch {
    return FALLBACK;
  }
}

const FALLBACK: Stats = { stars: null, downloads: null, release: "v0.17" };
```

Then in your Astro page frontmatter:

```astro
---
import { fetchStats, formatCount } from "../lib/stats";
const stats = await fetchStats();
---
<span data-stat="stars">{formatCount(stats.stars)}</span> stars
<span data-stat="downloads">{formatCount(stats.downloads)}</span> downloads
```

The `cache` module-level promise memoizes within a single build, so all 9 locale pages we generate share one network round-trip rather than hammering GitHub nine times. The `data-stat` attribute is the hook Layer 3 will use to update in place.

## Layer 2 — Edge proxy

A Cloudflare Pages Function (or Vercel Edge Function, or Netlify Edge Function) serves `/api/stats` from the same domain as the site. Browsers never call api.github.com directly, so:

- The unauth rate limit is consumed once per 5-minute window per region, not once per visitor.
- CORS is a non-issue — same origin.
- If you want to add an authenticated GitHub PAT to lift the rate limit, it lives as one env var on the edge — never in browser code.

```ts
// web/functions/api/stats.ts (Cloudflare Pages Function)
const SUCCESS_MAX_AGE = 300; // 5 min
const FAILURE_MAX_AGE = 30;  // 30 s — IMPORTANT, see footgun #2

export const onRequestGet: PagesFunction<{ GITHUB_TOKEN?: string }> = async (ctx) => {
  const cacheKey = new Request("https://internal/__stats_v1", { method: "GET" });
  const cache = caches.default;
  const cached = await cache.match(cacheKey);
  if (cached) return cached;

  const res = await buildResponse(ctx.env);
  ctx.waitUntil(cache.put(cacheKey, res.clone()));
  return res;
};

async function buildResponse(env): Promise<Response> {
  const headers: Record<string, string> = {
    "User-Agent": "your-site",
    Accept: "application/vnd.github+json",
    ...(env.GITHUB_TOKEN ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${env.GITHUB_TOKEN}` } : {}),
  };
  try {
    const [r1, r2] = await Promise.all([
      fetch("https://api.github.com/repos/<you>/<repo>", { headers,
        cf: { cacheTtl: SUCCESS_MAX_AGE, cacheEverything: true } }),
      fetch("https://api.github.com/repos/<you>/<repo>/releases?per_page=100",
        { headers, cf: { cacheTtl: SUCCESS_MAX_AGE, cacheEverything: true } }),
    ]);
    if (!r1.ok || !r2.ok) return failureResponse();
    // ... reduce downloads, build body ...
    return new Response(JSON.stringify(body), {
      status: 200,
      headers: {
        "content-type": "application/json",
        "cache-control": `public, max-age=${SUCCESS_MAX_AGE}, s-maxage=${SUCCESS_MAX_AGE}`,
      },
    });
  } catch {
    return failureResponse();
  }
}

function failureResponse(): Response {
  return new Response(
    JSON.stringify({ stars: null, downloads: null, release: null }),
    {
      status: 200,  // NOT 503 — see footgun #1
      headers: {
        "content-type": "application/json",
        "cache-control": `public, max-age=${FAILURE_MAX_AGE}, s-maxage=${FAILURE_MAX_AGE}`,
      },
    });
}
```

## Layer 3 — Client refresh

A tiny inline script that runs after page interactive, fetches `/api/stats`, and updates the chips in place — but only if the answer is `> 0`:

```js
(function () {
  function fmt(n) {
    if (n === null || !Number.isFinite(n)) return "—";
    if (n < 1000) return String(n);
    if (n < 10000) return (n / 1000).toFixed(1).replace(/\.0$/, "") + "k";
    return Math.round(n / 1000) + "k";
  }
  function paint(key, value) {
    if (typeof value !== "number" || value <= 0) return;  // FOOTGUN #1
    document.querySelectorAll('[data-stat="' + key + '"]')
      .forEach(el => el.textContent = fmt(value));
  }
  fetch("/api/stats")
    .then(r => r.ok ? r.json() : null)
    .then(d => { if (d) { paint("stars", d.stars); paint("downloads", d.downloads); } })
    .catch(() => {});
})();
```

## The two footguns we've eaten

### Footgun #1 — null vs 0 must be distinguished

On any failure path — Layer 1's build fetch, Layer 2's edge fetch — return `null`, not `0`. Then the client-side painter checks `> 0` rather than `!= null` before overwriting. Otherwise: a single GitHub 503 happens, your edge proxy returns `{stars: 0}`, that gets cached for 5 minutes across every region, and your homepage proudly displays "⭐ 0 stars · 0 downloads" while everyone wonders if you abandoned the project. The fix took 4 minutes; the trust took longer.

### Footgun #2 — failure responses need a short cache TTL

Success: cache for 300 seconds (or whatever your refresh budget is). Failure: cache for 30 seconds, or don't cache at all. A bad answer pinned to the edge for 5 minutes is far worse than re-asking too soon. The `SUCCESS_MAX_AGE` / `FAILURE_MAX_AGE` split in the Layer 2 snippet above does exactly this.

## Other framework adapters

The pattern's the same — build-time + edge proxy + client refresh — only the function signatures differ.

- **Next.js**: build-time = `getStaticProps` / Server Component. Edge proxy = `app/api/stats/route.ts` with `export const runtime = "edge"`.
- **Vercel**: drop the proxy file at `api/stats.ts` with `export const config = { runtime: "edge" }`. Caching via `Cache-Control` headers; Vercel respects them.
- **Netlify**: `netlify/edge-functions/stats.ts` with the same headers. `Deno.env` for the optional GitHub token.
- **SvelteKit**: `+server.ts` in the route folder, mark with `export const config = { runtime: "edge" }`.
- **Hugo / Jekyll / Eleventy**: only Layer 1 + Layer 3, no Layer 2 (these are pure static; you'd need a separate edge function on whatever CDN you front them with).

## One bonus pattern

A desktop app's auto-update check should hit your `/api/stats` (or a sibling `/api/latest-release`) for the same reason: don't make a million installs hammer api.github.com directly. Same edge cache, same rate limit savings. Unterm's own update poller does this.

---

Reference implementation lives in [github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/tree/master/web](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/tree/master/web) — `functions/api/stats.ts` for Layer 2, `src/lib/stats.ts` for Layer 1, `src/layouts/Base.astro` for the inline Layer 3 script. MIT-licensed, copy what you need.

# Unterm v0.71.22: Unterm Pocket 移动端网关、Agent Harness、主屏重排与 xterm 网格对齐

Source: https://unterm.app/blog/mobile-harness-reflow-v07122-zh

> English version: [Unterm v0.71.22: Unterm Pocket, Agent Harness, Main-Screen Reflow & xterm Grid Alignment](/blog/mobile-harness-reflow-v07122/)

**Unterm v0.71.22** 带来了两条核心工程演进：

1. **Unterm Pocket 与 Agent Harness（`unterm-cli remote`）**——纯本地优先的局域网 / Tailscale 移动端远程网关，支持扫码配对与三级权限控制、本地开发服务器端口发现与反向代理预览、零污染隐藏 Git 检查点、跨 Agent 便携交接以及窗口 + A11y 控件树快照。
2. **主屏重排（Reflow）与 xterm 网格对齐**——宽度变化时自动重排软换行、高度缩小时保留光标所在行、全面对齐 xterm / ECMA-48 网格与光标语义，以及严格按单元格边界定位与裁切字形。

---

## 1. Unterm Pocket：局域网 / Tailscale 手机端远程驾驶舱

当 AI 编程 Agent 正在执行耗时任务时，开发者经常需要在离开电脑时用手机查看终端输出、审批高风险操作，或在真机上预览本地开发服，但又不希望终端数据经过任何第三方云端中转。

在 v0.71.22 中，Unterm 推出了 **Unterm Pocket**（可通过 `unterm-cli remote` 或 Web Settings 中的 **Remote / Mobile** 标签页开启）：

- **严格限定局域网与 Tailscale**：在 Socket 层直接拒绝非私有局域网（RFC1918）与非 Tailscale（`100.64.0.0/10`）网段的连接请求，绝不暴露公网。
- **一次性 6 位配对码与二维码**：配对码有效期 2 分钟且单次有效，配对后基于 Ed25519 主机密钥与 SHA-256 哈希令牌持久化设备授权，随时可一键吊销。
- **三级权限范围（`full` / `approve` / `readonly`）**：
  - `readonly`（只读监看）：仅允许查看实时终端屏幕、回滚历史与检查点列表，禁止一切写入；
  - `approve`（仅审批与对话）：允许审批/拒绝 Agent 操作并发送对话输入，但拦截信号发送与回滚；
  - `full`（完全控制）：开放全部远程驾驶舱能力，包含检查点恢复与窗口快照。

---

## 2. Agent Harness：本地预览代理、隐藏 Git 检查点与跨 Agent 交接

围绕多 Agent 协作与演进安全，v0.71.22 在 Web Settings、手机端与 `unterm-cli remote` 中同步落地了四大 Agent Harness 能力：

1. **本地开发服务器端口发现与预览代理（`/preview/<port>/`）**：自动扫描本机正在监听的 Web 开发端口（如 `:3000`、`:4321`、`:5173`、`:8080`），手机端配对后可直接通过内置反向代理一键打开预览。
2. **零污染隐藏 Git 检查点（`refs/unterm/checkpoints/<id>`）**：利用临时索引（`GIT_INDEX_FILE`）、`git write-tree` 与 `git commit-tree` 将当前工作区（含未跟踪新文件）完整快照至隐藏引用 `refs/unterm/checkpoints/<id>`，完全不触碰 `HEAD`、`.git/index` 或工作区状态；执行回滚前还会自动生成安全备份检查点。
3. **跨 Agent 便携交接包（`~/.unterm/handoffs/`）**：在严格保留用户新指令的前提下，按 Token 预算自动截取最近终端输出与 Git 状态摘要，生成标准 Markdown 交接文件，方便在 Claude Code、Codex CLI 与 Gemini CLI 之间无缝接力。
4. **窗口 + A11y 控件树快照（`~/.unterm/snapshots/`）**：一键捕获前台窗口截图（`.png`）与 UI Automation / System Events 无障碍控件树（`.a11y.json`），并生成可直接粘贴给 Agent 的结构化提示词片段。

---

## 3. 主屏软换行重排（Reflow）与 xterm 网格语义对齐

在终端分屏或调整窗口大小时，软换行文本如果不能随之重排，就会导致历史输出被截断或错位。v0.71.22 在 `unterm-engine` 中实现了完整的**主屏重排**：

- **逻辑行拼接与重折行**：窗口宽度变化时，将软换行连接的物理行还原为逻辑行，再按新列宽重新折行，完整保留硬换行、CJK 宽字符、字形簇与 SGR 样式属性。
- **高度缩小时保护光标行**：当窗口高度缩小时，优先将顶部行推入回滚缓冲区，确保光标所在行始终留在可视区域内。
- **全面对齐 xterm / ECMA-48 边界语义**：
  - 软换行标记归属行级（`ICH`/`DCH`/`ECH`/`SL`/`SR`/`EL 1`/`DECERA`/`DECFRA`/`DECSERA` 保留，`EL 0`/`EL 2`/`ED`/`DECSED` 清除）；
  - `DECLRMM` 左右边距与上下滚动区的光标移动及钳位规则与 xterm 完全一致；
  - `DECFRA` / `DECERA` / `DECSERA` 矩形区域指令在边界处自动拆分跨界宽字符；
  - 同步输出模式（`CSI ? 2026 h/l`）提升为全局状态，跨主/备用屏切换与视口滚动期间均保持生效；
  - `LF` / `VT` / `FF` 默认保留光标列坐标，并完整实现 `LNM`（`CSI 20 h/l`）换行模式。

---

## 4. 单元格级字形定位裁切与 Windows 零闪烁启动

- **按源单元格定位、反色与裁切字形**：`unterm-render` 严格按照字形簇所属的单元格计算坐标、块状光标反色与裁剪矩形，并将 HarfBuzz 26.6 塑形偏移四舍五入至整像素，杜绝超宽图标侵入右侧相邻字符。
- **回滚长图宽字符步进修复**：修复回滚 PNG 渲染器未跳过宽度为 0 的宽字符延续格、导致中文字符前进 3 列的问题。
- **Windows 启动零闪烁**：在 `ShowWindow` 前强制同步施加 `LWA_ALPHA=0` 分层透明与 DWM Cloak，直到首帧 GPU 画面提交后再揭开窗口，彻底消除启动瞬间的黑影或白框闪烁。

---

## 立即升级

直接运行 `unterm-cli update`，或通过 Homebrew（`brew upgrade --cask unterm`）、Scoop（`scoop update unterm`）及 [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/releases/tag/v0.71.22) 下载升级。

---

# Unterm v0.71.22: Unterm Pocket, Agent Harness, Main-Screen Reflow & xterm Grid Alignment

Source: https://unterm.app/blog/mobile-harness-reflow-v07122

> 中文版: [Unterm v0.71.22: Unterm Pocket 移动端网关、Agent Harness、主屏重排与 xterm 网格对齐](/blog/mobile-harness-reflow-v07122-zh/)

**Unterm v0.71.22** ships two major tracks of engineering:

1. **Unterm Pocket & Agent Harness (`unterm-cli remote`)** — a local-first LAN / Tailscale mobile gateway with scoped permissions, localhost dev-server reverse proxying, zero-pollution hidden Git checkpoints, cross-agent handoffs, and foreground window + Accessibility (A11y) snapshots.
2. **Main-Screen Reflow & xterm Grid Alignment** — soft-wrap line reflow on width changes, cursor-preserving height shrink, strict xterm/ECMA-48 grid semantics (`DECLRMM`, `DECFRA`/`DECERA`/`DECSERA`, global `?2026`, `LNM`, `XTSAVE`/`XTRESTORE`), and per-cell glyph placement and clipping.

---

## 1. Unterm Pocket & Scoped Mobile Remote Access

When an AI coding agent is running a long task, you often want to monitor its progress, approve a gated action, or preview a dev server from your phone without routing your terminal through a third-party cloud relay.

In v0.71.22, Unterm introduces **Unterm Pocket** (`unterm-cli remote` and the **Remote / Mobile** tab in Web Settings):

- **LAN & Tailscale Only**: Connections are restricted at the socket layer to private RFC1918 LAN addresses and Tailscale (`100.64.0.0/10`) CIDRs.
- **One-Time 6-Digit Pairing & QR Code**: Pairing codes expire in 2 minutes and are consumed on first use, issuing an Ed25519-backed device record and SHA-256 hashed bearer token.
- **Three Permission Scopes (`full`, `approve`, `readonly`)**:
  - `readonly`: Watch live terminal panes, scrollback, and checkpoints without write access;
  - `approve`: Approve or reject pending agent actions and steer prompts, while blocking destructive signals or checkpoint rollbacks;
  - `full`: Full remote cockpit control, including localhost dev-server preview and checkpoint restoration.

---

## 2. Agent Harness: Preview Proxy, Hidden Git Checkpoints & Portable Handoffs

Alongside mobile access, v0.71.22 adds four Agent Harness primitives accessible from Web Settings, mobile devices, and `unterm-cli remote`:

1. **Localhost Dev-Server Discovery & Preview Proxy (`/preview/<port>/`)**: Automatically discovers listening local dev ports (`:3000`, `:4321`, `:5173`, `:8080`, etc.) and proxies them over your authenticated LAN/Tailscale session so you can test mobile layouts directly on your phone.
2. **Zero-Pollution Hidden Git Checkpoints (`refs/unterm/checkpoints/<id>`)**: Snapshots the entire working tree—including untracked files—using a temporary index (`GIT_INDEX_FILE`), `git write-tree`, and `git commit-tree`, storing the commit under `refs/unterm/checkpoints/<id>` without touching `HEAD`, `.git/index`, or `git status`. Restoring a checkpoint automatically creates a safety backup checkpoint first.
3. **Cross-Agent Portable Handoffs (`~/.unterm/handoffs/`)**: Packages a pane's recent terminal scrollback, Git status/diff summary, and your full new instruction into a token-budgeted Markdown bundle ready to hand off between Claude Code, Codex CLI, and Gemini CLI.
4. **Window + Accessibility (A11y) Snapshots (`~/.unterm/snapshots/`)**: Captures the foreground window PNG alongside its UI Automation / System Events Accessibility control tree (`.a11y.json`) and formats a one-line prompt snippet for visual debugging.

---

## 3. Main-Screen Reflow & xterm Grid Semantics

Resizing a terminal window or splitting a pane mid-session used to clip or misalign soft-wrapped lines. In v0.71.22, `unterm-engine` implements full **main-screen reflow**:

- **Logical Line Re-wrapping**: Soft-wrapped rows are rejoined into logical lines and re-wrapped to the new column width while preserving hard line breaks, wide CJK characters, grapheme clusters, and SGR attributes.
- **Cursor-Tracking Height Shrink**: When a window's height shrinks, the viewport scrolls excess top lines into scrollback rather than truncating the line the cursor sits on.
- **Strict xterm & ECMA-48 Alignment**:
  - Soft-wrap flags belong to the row (`ICH`, `DCH`, `ECH`, `SL`, `SR`, `EL 1`, `DECERA`, `DECFRA`, `DECSERA` preserve; `EL 0`, `EL 2`, `ED`, `DECSED` clear);
  - `DECLRMM` left/right margins and top/bottom scroll regions follow xterm cursor clamping rules;
  - `DECFRA` / `DECERA` / `DECSERA` cleanly split wide characters that straddle a rectangle boundary;
  - Synchronized output (`CSI ? 2026 h/l`) is now global state across main and alternate screens and holds during viewport scroll;
  - `LF` / `VT` / `FF` preserve the cursor column by default and support Line Feed / New Line Mode (`LNM`, `CSI 20 h/l`).

---

## 4. Per-Cell Glyph Placement, Clipping & Zero Startup Flash

- **Per-Cell Glyph Placement & Clipping**: `unterm-render` places, inverts, and clips glyphs strictly by the cell(s) their cluster belongs to, and rounds HarfBuzz 26.6 shaping offsets to the nearest pixel. Oversized icons no longer bleed into neighbouring columns.
- **Scrollback PNG Wide-Character Stride**: Fixed the scrollback PNG renderer so width-0 continuation cells are skipped and wide CJK characters advance 2 columns instead of 3.
- **Windows Zero-Flash Startup**: Enforces synchronous `LWA_ALPHA=0` layered cloaking and DWM cloaking before `ShowWindow` until the first GPU frame is presented.

---

## Upgrade Now

Run `unterm-cli update`, upgrade via Homebrew (`brew upgrade --cask unterm`) or Scoop (`scoop update unterm`), or download the latest release from [GitHub Releases](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/releases/tag/v0.71.22).

---

# Unterm v0.61:自研内核

Source: https://unterm.app/blog/next-core-v061-zh

> English version: [Unterm v0.61: our own kernel](/blog/next-core-v061/)

Unterm 起步于一个 WezTerm fork。对一个两个人的项目来说，这在当时是正确的选择——第一天就需要一个能用的终端，而 WezTerm 是一个出色的、久经考验的代码库。但那终究是为别人的目标构建的代码库：我们发的每一个 release，都背着几万行我们没写过、不需要、而且越来越要与之搏斗的代码。Agent Cockpit、屏幕读取、三套控制面——所有这些都是嫁接在一个从未为「被外部进程驱动」设计过的架构之上。

v0.61 终结了这次嫁接。fork 已从构建中彻底移除。Unterm 现在跑在 **next-core** 上——一个完全自研的终端内核。

## next-core 是什么

从你的按键到屏幕像素之间的一切:转义序列解析器、屏幕模型、回滚缓冲、Unicode 宽度处理、选区、pane 与会话、PTY 运行时、字体发现、栅格化与整形，以及基于 winit + wgpu 的 GPU 渲染器。全部是我们自己的代码，并被一条刻意设定的预算约束着:**约 12,000 行源码、10 个直接依赖**。这条预算不是用来炫耀的——它是我们强制执行的约束，让内核小到一个人能装进脑子里，而这正是「拥有它」的全部意义。

旧生态里只剩下两个工具 crate:`portable-pty` 和 termwiz 的 Unicode 表。两者都是叶子依赖，各自只做一件事。终端本身——决定「终端是什么」的那部分——不再有任何上游。

## 数字

同一台机器上实测，旧内核 vs next-core:

| 指标 | 之前 | v0.61 |
|---|---|---|
| 启动 → MCP 控制面就绪 | 7.1s | **22ms**(约 300 倍) |
| 提示符下的空闲 CPU | 单核 80% | **6.6%** |
| 20 万行输出洪泛 | 0.45s | 0.45s(持平) |
| Windows 安装版构建启动 | 1349ms | **761ms** |

对 Unterm 而言，最重要的是启动那个数字。当驱动面要花七秒才能出现时，「AI agent 可驱动的终端」多少带点期货性质——一个负责编排的 agent 每拉起一个窗口都要交这笔税。到了 22ms，生成一个终端比大多数 MCP 往返还便宜。Windows、吞吐、空闲占用全部持平或改善;没有为启动速度牺牲任何东西。

## 对齐是一本台账，不是一种感觉

替换一个成熟内核，危险的不是你重写的代码，而是你忘了曾经存在的行为。所以我们没有凭感觉发版。我们把旧内核的行为枚举成一本 **159 项需求台账**，逐项收口;另加一份 **29 项交互审计**，专查台账逮不住的东西:输出洪泛时拖拽选区会发生什么、组合输入进行到一半时 resize 后光标落在哪里、哪些修饰键组合能到达 shell。

排版也照此办理，按平台原生规范重建，而不是沿用 fork 时代的跨平台折中:macOS 红绿灯按钮放在系统规定的位置、pt = px 的字号规则与原生 app 所说的「13pt」一致、CJK 等宽正确性，以及按 CoreText 字重渲染字形——「为什么我终端里的字体比别处都细」这个 bug，在栅格化器层面修掉了。

## v0.61 还有

- **强制执行的命令白名单策略**——写入门禁现在是真正的策略引擎，不再只是一个确认对话框。
- **持久化的脱敏审计日志**——30 天 JSONL，token 已清洗，事后每一个 agent 动作都可追溯。
- **原生 macOS 交互式截图和文件夹选择器**——真正的系统组件，不是仿制品。
- **三层渲染管线**，模态浮层能正确合成在实时终端内容之上——TUI 跑着的时候不再有调色板闪烁。

## 拥有内核解锁了什么

到目前为止，我们发布的每个面向 agent 的功能都活在终端*之上*:读内核产出的屏幕、注入内核消费的输入。现在内核本身是我们的了，agent-first 的功能可以住进它*内部*——直接从模型输出结构化屏幕状态，而不是重新解析单元格;agent 可订阅的亚帧级损伤追踪;每 pane 的资源核算。而下一个平台原生的小毛刺出现时，修法是在我们自己写的 12,000 行里打一个 diff，不是对着别人的 roadmap 维护一条补丁队列。

真诚感谢 WezTerm 项目——fork 它是 Unterm 得以存在的原因;离开它是 Unterm 得以成为其所是的原因。

免费、MIT、本地优先、无账号、无遥测。[下载 v0.61](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/releases/latest) · [架构文档](/docs/architecture)

---

# Unterm v0.61: our own kernel

Source: https://unterm.app/blog/next-core-v061

> 中文版:[Unterm v0.61:自研内核](/blog/next-core-v061-zh/)

Unterm started as a fork of WezTerm. That was the right call for a two-person project that needed a working terminal on day one — WezTerm is an excellent, battle-tested codebase. But it's a codebase built for someone else's goals, and every release we shipped meant carrying tens of thousands of lines we didn't write, didn't need, and increasingly had to fight. The Agent Cockpit, screen reading, the three control surfaces — all of it was grafted onto an architecture that was never designed to be driven by external processes.

v0.61 ends the graft. The fork is gone from the build entirely. Unterm now runs on **next-core**, a terminal kernel written in-house.

## What next-core is

Everything between your keystrokes and the pixels: the escape-sequence parser, the screen model, scrollback, Unicode width handling, selection, panes and sessions, the PTY runtime, font discovery, rasterization and shaping, and a GPU renderer on winit + wgpu. All of it ours, held to a deliberate budget: **~12,000 source lines and 10 direct dependencies**. The budget isn't a brag — it's a constraint we enforce so the kernel stays small enough that one person can hold it in their head, which is the whole point of owning it.

From the old ecosystem, exactly two utility crates remain: `portable-pty` and termwiz's Unicode tables. Both are leaf dependencies doing one job each. The terminal itself — the part that decides what a terminal *is* — has no upstream anymore.

## The numbers

All measured on the same machine, old kernel vs. next-core:

| Metric | before | v0.61 |
|---|---|---|
| Launch → live MCP surface | 7.1s | **22ms** (~300×) |
| Idle CPU at a prompt | 80% of one core | **6.6%** |
| 200k-line output flood | 0.45s | 0.45s (parity) |
| Windows install-build start | 1349ms | **761ms** |

The startup number is the one that matters for what Unterm is. "The terminal AI agents can drive" was always slightly aspirational when the driving surface took seven seconds to exist — an orchestrating agent spawning a window paid that tax on every launch. At 22ms, spawning a terminal is cheaper than most MCP round-trips. Windows, throughput, and idle draw all held or improved; nothing was traded away for the startup win.

## Parity is a ledger, not a feeling

The dangerous part of replacing a mature kernel isn't the code you rewrite — it's the behavior you forget existed. So we didn't ship on vibes. We enumerated the old kernel's behavior into a **159-requirement ledger** and closed it item by item, plus a separate **29-item interaction audit** for the things ledgers miss: what happens when you drag-select during a flood, where the cursor lands after a resize mid-composition, which modifier combos reach the shell.

Typography got the same treatment, rebuilt to platform-native conventions instead of the fork's cross-platform compromises: macOS traffic lights where the OS puts them, pt = px sizing that matches what native apps mean by "13pt", CJK fixed-width correctness, and glyph rendering at CoreText weights — the "why does my terminal font look thinner than everywhere else" bug, fixed at the rasterizer.

## Also in v0.61

- **Enforced command allowlist policy** — the write-gate is now a real policy engine, not a confirmation dialog.
- **Persistent redacted audit trail** — 30 days of JSONL, tokens scrubbed, every agent action attributable after the fact.
- **Native macOS interactive screenshots and folder pickers** — the OS surfaces, not lookalikes.
- **A three-tier render pipeline** so modal overlays composite correctly over live terminal content — no more palette flicker over a running TUI.

## What owning the kernel unlocks

Every agent-facing feature we've shipped so far lived *above* the terminal: reading the screen the kernel produced, injecting input the kernel consumed. Now the kernel itself is ours, agent-first features can live *inside* it — structured screen state straight from the model instead of re-parsing cells, sub-frame damage tracking an agent can subscribe to, per-pane resource accounting. And when the next platform-native paper cut shows up, the fix is a diff in 12,000 lines we wrote, not a patch queue against someone else's roadmap.

Thanks to the WezTerm project — genuinely. Forking it is why Unterm exists; leaving it is why Unterm can become what it's for.

Free, MIT, local-first, no accounts, no telemetry. [Download v0.61](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/releases/latest) · [Architecture docs](/docs/architecture)

---

# Unterm v0.71.21: 彻底告别掉字、TUI 撕裂与界面卡顿

Source: https://unterm.app/blog/smooth-typing-ecma48-v071-zh

> English version: [Unterm v0.71.21: Zero Dropped Keystrokes, Flawless TUI Rendering](/blog/smooth-typing-ecma48-v071/)

在过去两周里，我们收到了一些资深用户与 AI Agent 开发者最硬核的真实反馈：
1. **打字飞快或者使用拼音/日文输入法选词时，偶发性丢掉一两个按键**；
2. **在跑 Claude Code、Antigravity (agy)、Bubble Tea 等复杂命令行工具时，一旦窗口尺寸变动或多行刷新，界面偶发整屏撕裂、提示符错位或光标乱跳**；
3. **在频繁分屏和切换标签页时，GUI 界面偶发停顿几十毫秒甚至半秒**。

这些问题往往不在基础基准测试里出现，却是在真正的开发者键盘上、在 AI 命令行高频调度的生产环境中让人心烦意乱的「暗礁」。

今天发布的 **Unterm v0.71.21**，带着我们对 Windows 消息系统底层、ECMA-48 国际终端规范与 GUI 帧缓存架构的深度重构，彻底收口了这些问题。

---

## 1. 消失的字符：Windows 消息队列与孤儿 WM_CHAR

在跨平台 Rust GUI 框架（如 `winit`）中，键盘事件通常被抽象为按键按下（`KeyDown`）、释放（`KeyUp`）与文本输入。然而 Windows 底层的 Win32 消息循环有着独特的时序机制：

当用户敲击键盘时，系统先产生 `WM_KEYDOWN`，随后由 `TranslateMessage` 产生字符消息 `WM_CHAR`。但在以下两种场景中，这个假定会破裂：
- **快速打字**：用户按键速度超过 100 WPM 时，`WM_KEYUP` 或下一个按键的 `WM_KEYDOWN` 极可能插队在 `WM_CHAR` 之前；
- **IME 选词上屏**：中文输入法候选词提交（Commit）瞬间，系统会瞬时向消息队列注入成串的合成字符消息。

如果事件循环按常规逻辑判定「该 `KeyDown` 未能立即匹配到有效物理字符」并直接丢弃，紧跟在后的 `WM_CHAR` 就会变成「孤儿消息」，导致用户屏幕上莫名其妙少了一个字母或汉字。

### 修复方案：双保险孤儿恢复机制

在 v0.71.21 中，我们重构了 Windows 输入通道：
1. **消息队列前瞻探查**：当捕获到 `Unidentified` 键位事件时，并不直接丢弃，而是通过 `recover_unidentified_windows_key` 探查 Win32 消息队列；
2. **虚拟键码保底回退**：若队列中没有待处理的 `WM_CHAR`，就从虚拟键码恢复字母和数字（`fallback_ascii_for_windows_vkey`）；
3. **去掉输入法上屏后的抑制窗口**：此前输入法提交后的一小段时间内，下一个按键会被丢弃，这段逻辑已移除。

**结果**：过去被 winit 报成 `Unidentified` 而丢掉的按键，现在都会送进 shell。

---

## 2. 撕裂的屏幕：ECMA-48 规范与 AI 命令行交互

现在越来越多的开发者开始把 AI Agent（例如 Claude Code、Google Antigravity CLI `agy`、Aider）作为日常开发主力。这类工具重度依赖现代 TUI 库（如 Go Bubble Tea、Rust reedline/crossterm、Python prompt_toolkit）进行动态多行渲染。

但不少用户反馈：**为什么调整终端窗口大小，或者 AI 吐出一大段代码时，屏幕会横向错位、光标乱跳，甚至把历史提示符覆写得一团糟？**

经过深度排查 VT100/ECMA-48 解析器，我们找到了罪魁祸首：

### (1) IL (Insert Lines) 与 DL (Delete Lines) 的光标列污染
当 TUI 需要在当前光标位置向上或向下滚动局部行块时，会发出 `CSI <n> L`（插入行）或 `CSI <n> M`（删除行）。
早期终端模拟器实现往往习惯性地把光标列（Column）顺便归零（回到行首）。然而根据 **ECMA-48 第 8.3.67 及 8.3.32 节标准规范**：
> *Insert Line / Delete Line 必须保持当前光标的列坐标绝对不变。*

顺便重置列坐标的错误行为，会导致后续紧跟的局部输出（如单字符属性高亮、输入框光标绘制）全盘向左偏移数格，引发毁灭性的横向排版撕裂！

### (2) 边界挂起折行（Pending Wrap）与退格越界
在终端行末输入最后一个字符时，终端处于「挂起折行」状态。若此时触发退格键（Backspace），如果边界判定偏移了一列，就会错误跳过行末文字甚至跳行擦除。
同时，当命令行向终端查询光标物理坐标（DSR 6n）时，若窗口刚好经历 Resize，返回的坐标可能短暂溢出当前行列界限，导致 TUI 框架崩溃或光标死锁。

在 v0.71.21 中，我们**严格对照 ECMA-48 标准修订了解析与屏幕缓冲区操作**：
- 严格保持 `IL` / `DL` 调用的列光标坐标；
- DSR 坐标返回前执行硬边界 Clamp 约束；
- 正确判定边界折行下的 Backspace 几何移动；
- 同步输出模式（Synchronized Output）下完备保护提示符与输入流。

现在无论你以多快的速度拖拽缩放窗口、无论 AI Agent 的代码流输出有多凶猛，屏幕渲染始终如丝般顺滑、严丝合缝。

---

## 3. 告别主线程卡顿：事件驱动的 FrameCache

在 Unterm 架构中，核心终端状态维护在独立的 Core 进程中，GUI 负责高帧率呈现。

在旧版本中，窗口在获取焦点或刷新会话列表时，GUI 线程偶尔会向 Core 发起同步 IPC 请求。一旦 Core 正在忙于刷入海量 PTY 吞吐，GUI 线程就会被动阻塞十几到数百毫秒，导致鼠标点击或快捷键响应出现轻微顿挫。

在 v0.71.21 中，会话状态的读取改走 **FrameCache**——一个事件驱动的客户端缓存：
- 缓存订阅 Core 的事件流，只有 Core 通知某个面板画面变化时才重新拉取；
- GUI 读取画面和会话列表都从本地内存取，不再每次读取都发一次同步 IPC；
- Core 忙于处理大量 PTY 输出时，UI 线程不再被它拖住。

---

## 4. 更多改进

- **Windows 11 无损截屏**：窗口截图（`capture.window`、`unterm-cli screenshot`）改用原生 DWM Cloaking 机制，截屏过程完全不抢夺用户焦点、不闪烁、不遮挡。
- **全平台一键安装升级**：已全量同步到 Homebrew、Scoop 与 GitHub Releases，全平台 9 大原生二进制安装包开箱即用。

---

## 立即体验

如果你已经在使用 Unterm，只需在终端中运行：
```bash
unterm-cli update
```
或者使用包管理器全新安装：
```bash
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install --cask zhitongblog/tap/unterm

# Windows (Scoop)
scoop bucket add zhitongblog https://github.com/zhitongblog/scoop-bucket
scoop install unterm
```

欢迎在 [GitHub Issues](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/issues) 与 [Discussions](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm/discussions) 中向我们反馈你的使用体验！

---

# Unterm v0.71.21: Zero Dropped Keystrokes, Flawless TUI Rendering

Source: https://unterm.app/blog/smooth-typing-ecma48-v071

> 中文版: [Unterm v0.71.21: 彻底告别掉字、TUI 撕裂与界面卡顿](/blog/smooth-typing-ecma48-v071-zh/)

Over the past few weeks, power users and AI agent developers surfaced three real-world rough edges:
1. **Occasional dropped keystrokes** when typing at high speeds or committing CJK IME candidate phrases on Windows;
2. **Horizontal tearing, ghost prompt duplication, or errant cursor jumps** during multi-line rendering in modern TUI applications (Claude Code, Google Antigravity `agy`, Bubble Tea, reedline) when resizing windows or streaming output;
3. **Subtle micro-stalls on the GUI thread** during rapid window focusing or pane switching under heavy output.

None of these showed up in basic synthetic benchmarks, but in daily production workflows with AI coding agents, they were noticeable pain points.

**Unterm v0.71.21** eliminates these issues with deep architectural fixes in the Windows message queue layer, strict ECMA-48 protocol compliance, and an event-driven frame cache between the GUI and the Core.

---

## 1. The Ghost Keystroke: Win32 Message Queues and Orphaned WM_CHAR

Cross-platform Rust GUI frameworks (such as `winit`) model keyboard input cleanly as KeyDown, KeyUp, and text input events. However, the Win32 message loop has subtle timing characteristics:

When a key is struck, Windows posts `WM_KEYDOWN`, and `TranslateMessage` subsequently posts `WM_CHAR`. But under two very common scenarios:
- **Fast typing (100+ WPM)**: `WM_KEYUP` or the next key's `WM_KEYDOWN` can interleave ahead of the pending `WM_CHAR`;
- **IME candidate commits**: Chinese/Japanese IME composition commit sends bursts of synthesized characters into the message queue.

If an event loop observes an `Unidentified` key without an immediate character payload and drops it, the trailing `WM_CHAR` is orphaned and lost, resulting in dropped letters or punctuation.

### The Fix: Double-Guard Orphan Recovery

In v0.71.21:
1. **Message Queue Lookahead**: On receiving an unidentified key event, `recover_unidentified_windows_key` inspects the Win32 message queue for pending `WM_CHAR` entries;
2. **Virtual-Key Fallback**: If no `WM_CHAR` is pending, letters and digits are recovered from the virtual-key code (`fallback_ascii_for_windows_vkey`);
3. **No Post-IME Suppression**: Removed the time window after an IME commit during which the next keystroke was discarded.

**Result**: keystrokes that winit used to report as `Unidentified` and drop are now delivered to the shell.

---

## 2. Screen Tearing in TUIs: Strict ECMA-48 Compliance

Developers increasingly drive AI coding agents (Claude Code, `agy`, Aider) directly in their terminal. These tools rely heavily on modern TUI libraries (Go's Bubble Tea, Rust's crossterm/reedline, Python's prompt_toolkit) for rich multi-line streaming and live progress bars.

When resizing the terminal or streaming verbose multi-line code diffs, users previously reported occasional visual tearing or misaligned prompts.

Our VT100 / ECMA-48 audit pinpointed the root causes:

### (1) Cursor Column Reset on IL (Insert Line) and DL (Delete Line)
When TUIs scroll a partial block of lines within the viewport, they issue `CSI <n> L` (Insert Line) or `CSI <n> M` (Delete Line).
Many terminal emulators erroneously reset the cursor column to 0 as part of this operation. However, **ECMA-48 §8.3.67 and §8.3.32 explicitly mandate**:
> *Insert Line and Delete Line must leave the cursor column position unaltered.*

Resetting the column caused subsequent partial redrawing (e.g. status tags or inline autocomplete) to shift leftward, causing horizontal tearing across the screen.

### (2) Pending-Wrap Boundaries and Clamped DSR Reports
When typing to the final column of a terminal row, the terminal enters a "pending-wrap" state. An off-by-one boundary check during backspaces could inadvertently skip characters or delete across row boundaries.
Furthermore, Device Status Report (DSR 6n) cursor coordinate queries now strictly clamp returned positions to the active screen geometry, preventing TUI layout engines from panicking during fast window resizes.

In v0.71.21:
- Cursor column is strictly preserved across `IL` / `DL` operations;
- DSR cursor position responses are boundary-clamped;
- Backspaces in pending-wrap states preserve exact character geometry;
- Synchronized Output (Mode 2026) ensures atomic redraws without ghost flicker.

---

## 3. Zero GUI Stalls: an Event-Driven FrameCache

In Unterm's architecture, the terminal core engine runs in an isolated daemon while the GUI renders through wgpu.

Previously, certain GUI operations (like window focus updates or session enumerations) made synchronous queries to the Core process. If the Core was busy streaming massive PTY throughput, the GUI main thread could experience a slight hitch.

In v0.71.21, we moved session state reads onto **`FrameCache`**, an event-driven client-side cache:
- The cache subscribes to the Core's event feed and refetches a pane only when the Core says its screen changed;
- The GUI reads screens and the session list from local memory instead of making a synchronous IPC call per read;
- The UI thread no longer waits on the Core when it is busy streaming heavy PTY output.

---

## 4. More Improvements

- **Win11 Native DWM Cloaking for Screen Capture**: Window screenshots (`capture.window`, `unterm-cli screenshot`) now use native DWM cloaking, eliminating window flicker or focus loss.
- **Cross-Platform Packages Ready**: Updated across Homebrew, Scoop, and GitHub Releases with native notarized DMG, Windows MSI/ZIP, and Linux AppImage/DEB.

---

## Getting Started

To update an existing installation:
```bash
unterm-cli update
```

To install freshly via package managers:
```bash
# macOS (Homebrew)
brew install --cask zhitongblog/tap/unterm

# Windows (Scoop)
scoop bucket add zhitongblog https://github.com/zhitongblog/scoop-bucket
scoop install unterm
```

Report any issues or join discussions on [GitHub](https://github.com/zhitongblog/unterm).
